fixes.explanation: I get why you'd picture something grand, friend, since David constructs buildings for himself in the same verse. But the text says he prepared a place for the ark and “…pitched a tent for it.” A tent, not a stone temple. Same ark, humbler roof.

The elders do show up later, going along with David with rejoicing (1 Chronicles 15:25). But carrying the ark isn't their job. David's rule names one group only: the Levites. Going along with the ark and carrying it are two different jobs.

A chariot would make for a fast entrance, friend. But the text says the Levites carried the ark “…on their shoulders with the poles…” No horses are mentioned anywhere. Shoulders and poles, as Moses had commanded.

That's right, friend. The Levites carry the ark “…as Moses had commanded in accordance with the word of the LORD.” Moses was Israel's leader long before David's day (Exodus 3:10). Carrying it this way wasn't a new idea. It was an old command being followed.

Runners would get the word out fast, friend. But the verse says these relatives are appointed “…as singers to lift up their voices…” That's the job the text gives them. The harps, lyres and cymbals go along with the singing.

Sorrow doesn't fit this plan, friend. The verse says the singers are to lift up their voices “with joy.” That's a day for celebrating. The sad songs can stay in the back of the junk drawer I got called out of years ago.

That's right, friend. The text says that “…God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD…” There's no anger this time, only help. And in that same verse, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.

I can see why you'd think the king would stand out, but it's actually True. The text says David “…was dressed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark…” The Levites match him. The text also says David wore a linen ephod.

This is a day of rejoicing, friend, but the text doesn't mention weeping at all. It says Michal “…saw King David dancing and celebrating…” That's what she sees from the window. Dancing and celebrating is the answer the verse gives.

The priests are busy in this passage, but the text never shows them arguing. Zadok and Abiathar are named earlier, and priests blow the trumpets before the ark (1 Chronicles 15:24). What Michal sees from the window is “…King David dancing and celebrating…” The only sour thing in the verse is what she feels in her heart.
